title: Changelog entries cannot preserve an intended release date
reasoning: The Changelog date is defined with auto_now_add, so Django always stores the row creation date and makes the field non-editable in normal model/admin forms. For a changelog, this prevents admins, data imports, or backfills from recording the actual release date when it differs from the database insertion date, causing displayed history to be wrong for delayed or historical entries.
recommendation: Replace auto_now_add=True with an explicit DateField default such as django.utils.timezone.localdate, or another project-appropriate default, while keeping the field editable so release dates can be corrected or backfilled.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: app_management/tests.py is empty, and the included context tests exercise hub/Fast behavior rather than Changelog creation or admin editing semantics.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a Changelog model test that creates an entry with an explicit historical date and asserts the stored date is preserved.
minimumFixScope: Update Changelog.date and add a migration altering the field default/editability.
